scenes.heading: Data Quality
scenes.narration: Data quality measures how well data serves its purpose across dimensions like accuracy, completeness, and timeliness.

scenes.heading: The dimensions of quality
bullets: Timeliness: data is fresh enough to trust.
scenes.narration: Accuracy asks whether the numbers are actually correct, while completeness asks whether anything is missing. Consistency checks that the same fact matches wherever it appears, and timeliness confirms the data is recent enough to be useful. Together these dimensions define what fit-for-purpose really means.

scenes.heading: Managing quality continuously
scenes.narration: You begin by defining measurable quality rules tied to business needs. Automated checks then score the data against thresholds on every run. When a metric slips you alert and remediate, and tracking the trend over time reveals whether quality is improving or decaying.

scenes.heading: A freshness and completeness check
scenes.code:
SELECT
  MAX(loaded_at)                                   AS last_load,
  COUNT(*)                                          AS row_count,
  AVG(CASE WHEN email IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)    AS null_email_rate
FROM daily_orders
WHERE loaded_at >= CURRENT_DATE;
scenes.narration: This query surfaces three quality signals in one pass. The last load timestamp reveals freshness, the row count exposes unexpected drops in volume, and the null rate flags completeness problems in a key field. Feeding these metrics into alerts turns quality from a hope into a monitored guarantee.

scenes.text: Data quality is a measurable, ongoing discipline spanning accuracy, completeness, consistency, and timeliness, not a one-time cleanup.
scenes.narration: Treat quality as a monitored metric with thresholds and alerts, and problems surface while they are still small and fixable.
